articles.title: ‘Woman Unknown’ Breakout Mathilde Arcel on Her Venice Award-Winning Performance and Life After Her Lido Triumph: ‘Everything Is Open’
articles.summary: Danish actress Mathilde Arcel would be the first to admit she didn’t see this coming. It’s been hardly two months since Arcel, in her first-ever leading role in a feature film, was awarded the Volpi Cup for best actress for her breakout performance in “Woman Unknown,” May el-Toukhy’s riveting…
body: Now, on the eve of the closing ceremony of the Thessaloniki Film Festival, which wraps Nov. 15 with el-Toukhy’s Venice winner, Arcel is taking in the news that she’s among the six nominees for best actress at the European Film Awards, whose nominations were announced Saturday afternoon in Thessaloniki.
For Arcel, whose grandmother comes from the Greek island of Lesvos, the award ceremony, which will be held in Athens in January, feels like “a weird kind of homecoming.”

Over coffee at Thessaloniki’s Mediterranean Palace, the 30-year-old still seems awestruck by her meteoric rise. Just over two months ago, Arcel was herself a relative unknown, with a career that had mostly spanned the stage and television. Before her Venice breakout, her only appearances on the big screen were in supporting roles.

After accepting best actress honors on the Lido, Arcel revealed to Danish media that she’d been collecting unemployment benefits ahead of the Italian fest; she was on her way to report to a job center in Copenhagen when she got word that she needed to fly back to Venice for the award ceremony.

articles.title: ‘Dhurandhar,’ ‘Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1’ Among Indian Panorama Lineup at IFFI Goa
articles.summary: Aditya Dhar’s Hindi-language “Dhurandhar” will open the Indian Panorama section of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Rishab Shetty’s Kannada-language “Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1” is also in the lineup.
body: “Dhurandhar” and “Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1” both sit in the five-title Mainstream Cinema strand. They are joined there by Samir Tewari’s Marathi-language film “Baapya,” Anil Ravipudi’s Telugu-language title “Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu (Pandaga Ki Vastunnaru)” and Pravin Vitthal Tarde’s “Deool Band 2,” also in Marathi.

A 12-member jury chaired by Indian National Film Award-winning filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar picked the features from 404 submissions. The other 20 titles cover 12 languages, from Hindi, Tamil and Bengali to Tulu and Nyishi.

Among them are Kamakhya Narayan Singh’s “The Kerala Story 2 Goes Beyond,” Bharatbala Ganapathy’s “Banaras,” Akhil Sathyan’s Malayalam film “Sarvam Maya,” P. Sheshadri’s Kannada title “Ruby-Cube” and Singeetham Srinivasa Rao’s Telugu feature “Sing Geetham.” Sahil Shah’s “Birds on Ice,” in Ladakhi, and Duyu Tabyo’s Nyishi-language “Urum” also made the cut.

articles.title: Jakarta World Cinema Expands to Malang and Bandung, Where Palme d’Or Winner ‘Fjord’ Opens Festival
articles.summary: Jakarta World Cinema has taken its festival outside the Indonesian capital for the first time, with the inaugural Bandung World Cinema and Malang World Cinema opening simultaneously on Nov. 14 in two cities with large student populations and busy creative scenes.
body: The Bandung edition is programming 203 international titles drawn from 69 countries. Cristian Mungiu’s “ Fjord,” which won this year’s Palme d’Or at Cannes, opened proceedings.

Also on the slate are Beth de Araujo’s “Josephine,” which took both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award in Sundance’s U.S. Dramatic Competition in 2026, and Marine Atlan’s “La Gradiva,” winner of the AMI Paris Grand Prize at this year’s Cannes Critics’ Week. Sandra Wollner’s “Everytime,” which picked up the Un Certain Regard Prize at Cannes, screens alongside Kurosawa Kiyoshi’s new feature “The Samurai and the Prisoner,” a Cannes Premiere selection.

The festival’s online program, available until Nov. 21, includes Ildiko Enyedi’s “Silent Friend,” a Fipresci Prize winner at Venice in 2025, and Ilker Çatak’s “Yellow Letters,” this year’s Golden Bear winner at the Berlinale.
Bandung Mayor Muhammad Farhan attended the opening night at CGV Paris Van Java.

articles.title: Amanda Seyfried to Make Her Debut as ‘Saturday Night Live’ Host
articles.summary: Amanda Seyfried will make her debut as host of “Saturday Night Live” on Dec. 5. Seyfried is center stage in one of the year’s most talked-about movies, the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything.” The musical guest for the episode will be rapper Don Toliver.
body: Seyfried has a big role in A24’s “You Can See Everything” given her history of playing the convicted Theranos fraudster Holmes in the 2022 Hulu limited series “The Dropout.” Directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim tapped Seyfried to recreate some scenes in a meta approach to the doc that chronicles the final few weeks for Holmes before she begins her prison sentence for her conviction on multiple charges of wire fraud.

Seyfried recently completed the indie film “The Life and Deaths of Winston Shedd,” opposite Tim Blake Nelson. She’s also set to voice the lead role of Cinderella in Netflix’s upcoming animated film “Steps.” She had a busy year in 2025 with starring roles in two successful films, Paul Feig’s “The Housemaid” and Mona Fastvold’s “The Testament of Ann Lee.”

Seyfried earned an Oscar nomination for supporting actress for her work in David Fincher’s 2021 drama “Mank,” about screenwriter Herman Mankiewicz and the making of Orson Welles’ 1941 movie masterpiece “Citizen Kane.” She was nominated for an Emmy for her work in “The Dropout.”

articles.title: Alleged Russell Brand rape victim wants age of consent law changed
articles.summary: Mia Latter, who says she was 16 when she met the convicted rapist, wants a staggered age of consent.
body: Mia Latter was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. She was known under the pseudonym 'Alice'. Brand denied the allegations at the time.
None of the women in the 2023 media investigation were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.
Speaking to the Sunday Times, she added that it was "disgusting" that a culture existed in the 2000s that "normalised and celebrated" celebrities having relationships with teenagers.

On Monday the entertainer was sentenced to 10 and a half years for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two counts of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.

articles.title: 'It's like you're in one of his paintings' Kyffin Williams' art brought to life
articles.summary: Technology similar to that used for exhibitions of Van Gogh, Cézanne and LS Lowry is being used.
body: For the first time, the paintings of Sir Kyffin Williams have been brought to life in a new immersive experience at the National Library of Wales.

Images from Williams's oil paintings such as the hill farmer and sheepdog are animated in a 360-degree centrepiece and Sir Kyffin's life story is narrated by Sir Bryn Terfel in a bilingual presentation, with original paintings illuminated on the walls.
The National Library, which received grants of £500,000 to fund the project, said it hoped it will introduce a new audience to Sir Kyffin's work.
There are also interactive installations including a recreation of a self-portrait which can be touched, giving visitors a sense of the texture of Sir Kyffin's oil paintings.

articles.title: Listen to the River! ‘Arrow for a Stone Heart’ Is a Poetic Hybrid Experience Told Through an Indigenous Lens
articles.summary: Yes, a peccary in the forest near São Paulo is also talking to us in writer, director and cinematographer Luiza Calagian's debut feature premiering in Tallinn's Rebels With a Cause Competition - find out why.
body: A pig-like creature is walking around in the territory of the indigenous Guaraní on the outskirts of São Paulo, Brazil. “My name is Rete, I am a peccary,” it tells us. And it shares what started happening to nature back in the days when the colonizers began to settle. “One day, those who are many started arriving.” Over time, the stones they brought started swallowing up more and more space, restricting an ancient river, plants and many creatures.

In her poetic debut feature, Arrow for a Stone Heart ( Flecha para Um Coração de Pedra ), writer, director and cinematographer Luiza Calagian, in collaboration with the local Guaraní indigenous community, transport us into the heart of the forest near the city. And the documentary-fiction hybrid’s narrative is very different for a reason. The way the indigenous people experience and narrate reality is different. From their perspective, myths, dreams, and relationships with non-humans connect different temporalities and perspectives.

The cinematic, maybe even hallucinatory, journey that the movie takes us on elucidates the history of the community’s struggle. Cinema emerges as an opportunity for understanding and, possibly, change.

articles.title: Star-studded MacGowan tribute album gave grieving wife purpose
articles.summary: Three years after her husband's death, Victoria Mary Clarke's idea to put together a tribute album for her late husband came to fruition.
body: On the day of Shane MacGowan's funeral, his heartbroken wife found comfort in the same thing that moved and captivated the rest of the world that afternoon - the music that filled a parish church in Nenagh, County Tipperary.
Mundy and Camille O'Sullivan performed Haunted. Nick Cave sang A Rainy Night in Soho. And Glen Hansard and Lisa O'Neil led mourners in a send-off rendition of Fairytale of New York.
"I thought, well, if we just got all the people who were at the funeral on a record, that'd be something pretty special," Victoria Mary Clarke told BBC News NI.
On Friday, three years after her husband's death, that idea came to fruition with the release of 20th Century Paddy.

articles.title: Hannah Fry feels 'unbelievably lucky' after cervical cancer treatment
articles.summary: The presenter says she has received a 'five-year clear' after having a hysterectomy in her thirties.
body: Prof Hannah Fry has described feeling "unbelievably lucky" after being treated for cervical cancer.
The mathematician and BBC presenter, who recently took part in the second season of the Celebrity Traitors, said cancerous cells were discovered after she attended a cervical screening in 2020.
She underwent a hysterectomy, describing the experience to BBC Radio 4's Desert Island Discs as "horrific".
"As awful as that was, it had a full stop at the end of the sentence," the 42-year-old added. "I had my five-year clear the other day. I feel so unbelievably lucky."

articles.title: 10 Years Later, a ‘Game of Thrones’ Star’s $208M Gem Is Officially a Netflix Smash Hit
articles.summary: Emilia Clarke is best known for her role as Daenerys Targaryen in HBO's Game of Thrones, but her impressive catalog of movie and TV performances stretches far beyond Westeros.
body: The 2016 romantic comedy Me Before You, based on Jojo Moyes ’ bestselling novel, stars Clarke alongside Sam Claflin, as she becomes his caregiver following a tragic accident that leaves him paralyzed. The film received a positive response from critics and proved popular at the box office. Against a reported budget of $20 million, Me Before You earned an impressive $208 million worldwide, with more than $150 million made from overseas markets. Ten years later, it's a hit again. At the time of writing, Me Before You is one of the ten most-watched movies on Netflix in the world.

Me Before You is currently the seventh most-watched movie on Netflix in the world, so what are the six titles ranking higher? The recent horror hit Final Destination Bloodlines ranks in sixth place, with the Gene Hackman -led Heist in fifth, and the animated sequel Sing 2 in fourth. Third place currently goes to the new festive hit A Dog's Perfect Christmas, with the Brazilian comedy My Best Friend in second, and the Spanish thriller Collision Course topping the charts.
For the latest streaming stories, make sure to stay tuned to Collider.
